clips.verdict: Dead at 0 views after 116h; the premise is decent but it's too old and the channel isn't being served, so the pick can't be judged yet.
clips.worked: The narrator line is a clean one-sentence premise (a fan read a whole book on seduction to write a letter) and the fan-mail format is easy to understand cold.
clips.hurt: The hook 'WAIT FOR LIFE ADVICE' is a vague tease that promises advice, not a stake, and it clashes with the narrator's seduction framing. 53s is long for a letter being read aloud. The title spoils the topic but never says what Jynxzi does with it.
clips.better_title: Jynxzi Opens a Fan Letter Written After a Whole Book 😭
clips.better_hook: HE READ A WHOLE BOOK FOR THIS

clips.verdict: Early-distribution failure with 0 views; the pick itself is weak because it's mostly visual crowd chaos with no spoken premise.
clips.worked: Kai plus Ray is the strongest pairing in the niche, and the narrator line states a clear job (keep Ray safe).
clips.hurt: Fans following them is visual and crosstalk-heavy, so it depends on seeing the scene. The hook question 'CAN KAI GET RAY THROUGH?' is answered vaguely, and 53s dilutes it. The title is a command with no punchline.

clips.better_hook: KAI'S ONE JOB: KEEP RAY SAFE

clips.verdict: Near-zero views; a visual dog moment with a weak spoken premise, so skip this kind of pick.

titles: Creator name first, then the setup in plain verbs. Never put the result in the title (Red Card, Copper, Hang On).
Sell the joke the clip answers, e.g. 'Asks If This Dog Is Ever Happy', not trivia or the outcome.
Keep titles under 60 characters with 1-2 emoji at the end.
hooks: Max 6 words, written as the stake or question the clip answers within 15s (e.g. 'IF PALMER SCORES, STREAM ENDS').
Don't restate the narrator. If hook and narrator say the same thing, cut one. No mood labels or vague teases like 'WAIT FOR LIFE ADVICE'.
Ban 'and then this happened' in narrator lines; state the promise and stop.
clip_picks: Only pick moments with a one-line spoken premise (bet, guess, countdown, question). Speed and Kai crossovers with athletes or celebrities come first, then Kai with Ray.
Skip visual-only or crosstalk moments (fans chasing Kai, a clinch, a dog). If the transcript isn't funny read aloud, skip it.
Listen to the full clip for n-words before cutting; if muting kills the payoff, skip.
length_and_pacing: Stop cutting every clip to 53s. Start ≤2s before the stake line and end ≤2s after the payoff. Aim for 15-30s, since the breakouts are mostly 11-26s.
End on the payoff line and cut trailing banter so the clip loops cleanly.
posting: Post 1-2 clips a day within hours of the stream. Clips 5-7 days old compete with hundreds of other clippers.

All six clips sit at 0-15 views with n/a analytics, which points to distribution, not just picks. Check the channel for limits, duplicate-content flags and Shorts-feed serving before judging any clip.
After 48h, judge on 3s retention and Shorts-feed share, but only once Studio shows those numbers.

money.idea: Join paid clipping campaigns (N3on is the known one)
money.why: With 0 subs and 18 Shorts views, YPP is far away, and campaigns pay per clip or view without needing a subscriber base. Your streamer-clip format already matches.
money.first_step: Open the N3on campaign page, read the content rules and payout terms, and submit one short cut from an allowed source stream that fits the rules.

money.idea: Build toward fan funding and YPP by volume of short, tight clips
money.why: Fan funding needs 500 subs and 3M Shorts views, and full YPP needs 1,000 subs and 10M views. Breakouts in the niche reach millions at 11-26s, so fast, punchy cuts are the route to those thresholds.
money.first_step: Publish 7 clips of 15-30s this week from fresh streams, each with a one-line spoken premise, and track 3s retention in Studio.

money.idea: Add a pinned comment or description link to a streamer's own channel or a clip-friendly affiliate
money.why: This is a later option: once clips get views, a link to a relevant affiliate offer can earn a little. Don't pursue it until views exist.
money.first_step: Revisit once any single clip passes about 10,000 views, then check which programs the creators or fans around that clip actually use.

money.idea: Compile longer recap videos by creator (Kai in Japan, Speed vs athletes)
money.why: Long-form earns ad revenue under different rules than Shorts and lets you reuse the best moments once you have several.
money.first_step: Once you have 5+ good clips from a single stream, stitch them into one 8-10 minute recap and test it.

next_actions: Audit channel health in Studio: check for upload limits, copyright or duplicate-content flags, and whether any of the six clips appears in the Shorts feed. Do this before cutting anything new.
Retitle and re-hook the Speed vs Palmer clip (the only one with traction) and re-trim it to 15-30s if the platform allows it.
Cut the next 5 clips from fresh streams only (within hours), each 15-30s, with a spoken bet or guess premise and a hook that is a stake.
Prioritise Speed and Kai crossovers with athletes or celebrities and Kai with Ray over fan mail, dog, fight-clinch or crowd-chaos moments.
Apply to the N3on clipping campaign this week and read its rules before submitting.
